sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
The path was a steady mid-teens climb interrupted by a 6.9% year in FY2023, then re-acceleration to 15.7% in FY2024, 14.9% in FY2025 and 17.8% in FY2026 [D311][D364][D418][D472].
FY2026 revenue rose $50.1 billion or 18% driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud, with Intelligent Cloud led by Azure and Productivity and Business Processes by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud [P17].
The FY2023 slowdown came as revenue rose 7% on Intelligent Cloud and Productivity and Business Processes growth offset by a decline in More Personal Computing [P39].
Microsoft Cloud supplied 16.2pp of FY2026's 17.8% revenue growth and reached 64.6% of revenue [D568][D472][D566].
Server products and cloud services revenue rose $31.0 billion or 31% driven by Azure and other cloud services, whose revenue grew 41% [P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services revenue rose $14.2 billion or 16%, with cloud revenue up 17% on Copilot and E5 and seats up 6% [P14].
Operating income grew 20.8% against 17.8% revenue growth, an incremental operating margin of 53.3% [D473][D472][D498].
Operating costs grew 7.4% while revenue grew 17.8%, so operating costs grew 10.3pp slower than revenue, at 7.4% [D491][D472][D499].
Operating margin reached a window high of 46.8% in FY2026 against a 41.7% median and a 30.1% low in FY2017 [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin of 67.9% sat below its 68.2% median and 69.8% high, down 0.9pp on cost of revenue's 0.9pp drag [F30][D981][D980][D486][D500].
Intelligent Cloud gross margin percentage fell on continued AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, offset by Azure efficiency gains [P11].
In FY2026 net margin of 40.3% sat 6.5pp below the 46.8% operating margin, narrowed by $10.7 billion of other income [F70][F50][D1023][X124].
Other income included $6.5 billion of net gains on OpenAI investments, primarily the dilution gain from the OpenAI Recapitalization [P7].

Operating cash flow of $182.9 billion was 1.37x net income, in line with the 1.34x median, but free cash flow of $67.0 billion was only 0.50x, the window low [F100][F60][D459][D1013][F120][D460][D988].
Free cash flow margin fell to 20.2% from a 30.3% median as capex reached 34.9% of revenue and 3.38x D&A [D456][D984][D455][D461].
Cash used in investing rose $66.9 billion to $139.5 billion, primarily on a $51.4 billion increase in additions to property and equipment [P1].
Cash from operations rose $46.8 billion to $182.9 billion on higher cash received from customers and lower income tax payments [P1].
Net cash of $72.9 billion, 22.0% of revenue, ranked in the 83rd percentile of six software peers against a -7.2% median [D465][D466][D1006][D1007].
Total debt fell 6.6% to $40.3 billion while cash and investments rose 2.9% to $113.2 billion [D495][D464][D494][D463].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion plus dividends of $26.4 billion absorbed 72.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted count fell 0.2% [X147][X157][D468][D493].
The cushion is ample, but the 22.0% net cash ratio is well below the 53.8% of FY2018 as capex absorbs cash [D466][D40].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026, at 0.70x and 0.50x [R1][D406][D460].
The gap is capex-led rather than earnings-led, so it matters as a signal of how much AI infrastructure spending is consuming cash [D455].
Short-term investments were not reported in FY2017, so cash and investments and net cash omit them that year [R6][X158].
Any FY2017-to-FY2018 net cash comparison crosses that break and should not be read as a like-for-like change [R6].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers above the 20.2% FY2026 low or stays below the 30.3% median, in the FY2027 10-K [D982][D984].
Whether capex stays above 34.9% of revenue or falls back toward the 22.9% of FY2025, in the FY2027 10-K [D455][D401].
Whether operating margin holds above the 46.8% FY2026 high or slips toward the 41.7% median, in the FY2027 10-K [D974][D975].
